data.title: LASE to Premiere Quantum Bullet(TM) at Counter UAS Technology Conference in Washington, D.C.
data.description:
ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / LASE Corp. (NASDAQ:LASE), an emerging laser technology company developing laser and directed-energy solutions for the defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and industrial markets ("LASE" or the "Company"), today announced that it will premiere its Quantum Bullet™ anti-drone platform at Counter Unmanned Aircraft System ("UAS") Technology USA, taking place November 30 through December 2, 2026, in Washington, D.C., where Dmitri Nikitin, Executive Chairman of LASE Corp., will also present as a featured speaker.

This event brings together military, government and industry leaders to address the rapidly evolving threat posed by unmanned aerial systems and the technologies being developed to defeat them. This year's conference speakers include senior representatives of Joint Interagency Task Force 401 (JIATF-401), the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, the U.S. Army, the Air Force Research Laboratory, U.S. Northern Command and the Department of Homeland Security. Last year's conference drew attendees from more than a dozen countries, NATO, and allied ministries of defense, as well as leading defense contractors.

This premiere complements the Company's previously announced introduction of Quantum Bullet™ at the Interservice/Industry Training, Simulation and Education Conference (I/ITSEC), taking place November 30 through December 3, 2026, in Orlando, Florida.

The Quantum Bullet™ product line includes the Company's Laser Shield Anti-Drone ("LSAD") Series, a modular directed-energy platform being developed to address Group 1 and Group 2 drone threats. LSAD is designed to combine proprietary laser-based counter-drone capabilities with multi-sensor detection, tracking, targeting and command-and-control ("C2") systems supplied by LASE and its integration partners, supporting either standalone deployment or integration into multilayered air-defense networks.

LASE is developing LSAD as a modular offering that can be configured with different laser and power capabilities for different tactical scenarios. Its Dazzler configuration is intended to disrupt the optical and LIDAR sensors of Group 1 and Group 2 drones, while higher-energy palletized and crawler configurations, the latter designed for rapid all-terrain deployment, are being developed for destructive engagement of drone threats. Development, integration, testing and customer evaluation remain necessary before commercialization.

Dmitri Nikitin, Executive Chairman of LASE Corp said, "What we have developed with Quantum Bullet™ is a fundamentally different approach to counter-drone defense. It is designed to deliver the precision, effectiveness and cost efficiency needed to address one of the military's most urgent and widespread threats: Group 1 and Group 2 drones. But what makes Quantum Bullet™ particularly compelling is its versatility. It is not simply a standalone weapon. It is a modular, mobile and integrated defense platform designed to operate independently or as part of a larger, layered defense system."

Dmitri Nikitin continued, "We believe the future of counter-drone defense will depend on technologies that work together, adapt to evolving threats and can be deployed wherever our military needs them. That is exactly what we are building with Quantum Bullet™.

Mr. Nikitin, the Company's founder, brings more than three decades of experience in laser technology innovation spanning marking, cutting, welding, cleaning, glass separation and semiconductor processing. He co-developed the world's first high-power fiber laser cutting system and developed a first-of-its-kind mobile fiber-laser platform for military mine-clearing applications. Mr. Nikitin holds an engineering degree in industrial electronics and quantum mechanics from Moscow Power Engineering University and a Ph.D. from the Ministry of Electronics Industry of the USSR, and he is a named inventor on three patent applications relating to Bulk-to-Shape technology.

Quantum Bullet™ is a registered trademark with the USPTO.

For more information on LASE Corp. and its brands, please visit www.lase.com.

About LASE Corp.

LASE Corp. (NASDAQ:LASE), formerly Laser Photonics Corporation, is an emerging laser technology company developing laser and directed-energy solutions for the defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor and industrial markets. Through internal development, strategic acquisitions and partnerships, LASE intends to expand its technology portfolio, strengthen its advanced manufacturing capabilities and scale the enterprise profitably.

ROBOTERA Invited to APEC CEO Summit for Second Consecutive Year, Showcases Real-World Humanoid Robot Applications

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ROBOTERA, an AI-native embodied intelligence company, was invited to the 2026 APEC CEO Summit for the second consecutive year, becoming the only embodied intelligence company focused on real-world productivity to receive consecutive invitations. Founder and CEO Jianyu Chen and Co-founder Yue Xi attended the summit . Chen also delivered a keynote speech at APEC Finance Night titled "Putting Robots to Work at Night," sharing ROBOTERA's experience in turning embodied intelligence into practical productivity through real-world logistics deployments.

ROBOTERA has established deployments with China Post and SF Express, with its humanoid robots now operating across over 10 logistics centers. In these real-world operations, the robots achieve parcel induction rates exceeding 1,500 parcels per hour. By taking on repetitive, physically demanding tasks and challenging night shifts, they help address labor shortages while enabling human workers to focus on tasks requiring greater flexibility and judgment.

At the APEC CEO Summit, held from November 17 to 19, ROBOTERA showcased its humanoid robots and logistics solutions, including live parcel sorting demonstrations by its M7 humanoid robot. The demonstration gave international business leaders and attendees a firsthand look at how embodied intelligence is moving beyond technical demonstrations to deliver tangible value in real-world logistics operations.

data.title: European Midday Briefing: Shares Rise as Optimism Improves Ahead of Anthropic Trading Debut
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

Stocks:

European shares rose as tech sentiment rebounded after Anthropic raised $81 billion in its initial public offering, the biggest of all time.

Anthropic's trading debut will be in focus for the day ahead. "All outward signals suggest a lot of bullishness for the stock, which will be a major barometer of investors' appetite for risk in the AI-trade," said Capital.

Investors will also watch for readouts from the trilateral meeting between President Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.

Meanwhile, oil prices were mixed as the market weighed expectations of a surplus against continued threats to shipping in the Persian Gulf.

The International Energy Agency said Thursday that prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could substantially reduce the world's reliance on the waterway over the next decade as Middle Eastern producers develop alternative export routes.

U.S. Markets:

Stock futures were up as investors expressed optimism over Anthropic's IPO.

Investors were also digesting a hawkish tone struck in minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting.

Forex:

The euro was stable and the currency is consolidating below $1.10 as the strong dollar dominates across the board, ING said.

The dollar eased but stayed near the 19-month high reached overnight after the minutes of the Fed's latest meeting pointed to further interest rate rises. The rising possibility of the Fed increasing interest rates in quick succession at upcoming policy meetings is keeping the dollar strong, MUFG said.

Sterling traded flat. The Bank of England is expected to raise interest rates further to bring U.K. inflation down towards its 2% target and this should support sterling in the near term, Commerzbank said. Bonds:

Eurozone bond yields were slightly higher ahead of heavy bond supply from Spain and France.

Relief in French government bond yield spreads is still possible with the timely passage of a 2027 budget, even if by decree, ING said. Treasury yields turned higher as the minutes of the Fed's October meeting showed readiness to raise interest rates further, potentially at a faster pace.

Energy:

Oil prices were mixed. The IEA expects the global oil market to record a surplus of around 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter, widening to approximately 3.8 million barrels a day next year as Middle Eastern production recovers faster than demand.

Gas

European natural-gas prices rose in early trading following the previous session's drop, with the benchmark Dutch TTF contract now up 3.7% to 83.80 euros a megawatt hour.

Metals:

Gold prices continued to slip. "Minutes from the October [Federal Open Market Committee] showed strong alignment from Fed officials on the need for additional rate hikes," said MUFG.

Copper

Copper prices remained near their lowest level since April following a broad selloff across commodity markets, driven by a stronger U.S. dollar and growing concerns over AI-related investment.

EMEA HEADLINES

Houthi Attack Damages Saudi Capital's Tallest Tower

DUBAI-A projectile launched by Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi rebels struck the tallest tower in Saudi Arabia's capital Thursday, causing damage across multiple floors of a building home to the kingdom's sovereign-wealth fund.

The strike on the Public Investment Fund Tower, which stands over Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, follows a previous Houthi strike on the neighborhood that is home to some of the world's biggest financial firms.

UniCredit Strikes Deal With Germany to Clear Path for Commerzbank Takeover

UniCredit reached an agreement with the German government to resolve key issues in the takeover of Commerzbank, clearing the way for the Italian lender to take control of Germany's second-largest listed bank.

To meet Germany's demands, UniCredit agreed to keep Commerzbank's headquarters in Frankfurt, where the bank will remain listed on the stock exchange, according to a letter from UniCredit Chief Executive Officer Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil.

Deutsche Telekom's Tech Fund Invests $110 Million in Mistral AI

Deutsche Telekom's technology investment fund has invested around $110 million in Mistral AI as part of the French artificial-intelligence startup's Series D funding round.

The AI company completed its latest financing in September, raising a total of 3 billion euros ($3.29 billion) and lifting its valuation above 21 billion euros with backing from existing investors like Samsung Electronics and ASML Holding as well as new investors such as Advent, funds and accounts managed by BlackRock and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

Novartis Sees Sales Growth Through 2031

Novartis forecast steady sales growth through 2031, citing momentum from drugs already in the market and upcoming launches, and said medicines it has in the pipeline would help it sustain growth over the long term.

The Swiss drugmaker said Thursday that it expects annual sales growth of 5% from 2026 to 2031, excluding the effect of currency movements. It had previously forecast annual sales growth in the 5% to 6% range over the 2025-30 period.

GLOBAL NEWS

Wall Street Pledged to Mobilize $500 Billion for Nvidia-but Hasn't Put Up a Dime

Jensen Huang sensed the winds shifting against Nvidia this spring.

In June, Wall Street giants Apollo Global Management and Blackstone announced a megadeal to help Broadcom, one of Nvidia's main rivals, secure $35 billion of chip financing for Anthropic.

Trump, Xi and Putin Convene First-Ever Summit as World Order Shifts

SHENZHEN, China-President Trump was meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in this southern Chinese city on Thursday, in an unprecedented show of unity among the stewards of the world's three largest nuclear arsenals.

The first-ever gathering of the American, Chinese and Russian leaders is a further sign of the end of a unipolar world order dominated by the U.S.-and suggests that what might replace it is a more uncertain, and unsettled, reality.

Oil Prices Mixed as Traders Weigh Supply Outlook, Middle East Shipping Risks

DOHA, Qatar-Oil prices were mixed Thursday as traders assessed the global supply outlook amid continued threats to Middle Eastern oil shipments and fresh projections for the region's energy trade.

A top House Democrat issued document-preservation notices Wednesday to family members of President Trump and members of his administration, providing an early road map of potential targets of investigations next year.

The demands from Rep. Robert Garcia (D., Calif.), who is set to be the chairman of the Oversight Committee, focus on Trump family business ventures, the Department of Homeland Security's immigration enforcement, White House construction projects and documents related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Heavily armed insurgents in Iran's restive borderlands are posing a new challenge to the embattled leadership in Tehran, carrying out an increasing number of attacks in recent months that have targeted regime security forces.

data.description:
CTP Signs New Lease With Airbus at CTPark Brașov

Regulatory News:

CTP, Europe’s largest listed developer, owner and operator of logistics and industrial real estate by gross leasable area (GLA), has signed a new lease with Airbus, a leading aircraft manufacturer, for an 18,000 sqm Build-To-Suit facility at CTPark Brașov in Romania.

Airbus will use the high-quality energy efficient facility at CTPark Brașov for warehousing and logistics activities that enhance its operations. The deal brings one of the world’s most exceptional aerospace companies to CTP’s expanding business park community in Romania. It also marks an important milestone in CTPark Brașov‘s development, demonstrating its attractive strategic position for leading international companies.

Located to the north of Brașov in central Romania's Transylvania region, CTPark Brașov benefits from direct access to the DN13 motorway and is close to the city’s other main infrastructure including Brașov-Ghimbav International Airport. The park is also ideally located for businesses looking to establish or expand their operations in central Romania, with its position in one of the country's most established industrial and manufacturing regions with access to skilled labour, which was an important factor in Airbus’ decision to locate there.

The deal is also testament to the flexibility of CTP’s portfolio and its ability to provide major occupiers such as Airbus with both immediate solutions for space, and solutions for future expansion as needs evolve. With a network of parks across Romania and a portfolio spanning 12 European markets and an extensive landbank, CTP is ready to support clients with Grade A industrial and logistics properties, both in Romania and internationally. This is a key reason why over 70% of new leases CTP signs each year are with existing clients expanding across its network.

Ronald Binkofski, Managing Director, CTP Romania, said:

“We welcome Airbus to CTPark Brașov. One of the world’s most pioneering companies choosing to join CTP’s network demonstrates the quality of our Parks, the properties we deliver, and our capability to understand the needs of modern businesses. This is the latest in a series of leases we have signed with clients in Romania since the start of 2026, with more than 420,000 sqm of leases signed in the first nine months of the year, supported by demand for strategically located industrial and logistics space, continued growth in domestic consumption, and supply chain modernisation.”

Viorela Olteanu, Business Developer, CTP Romania, said:

“Airbus locating at CTPark Brașov is an important milestone for the park and a strong endorsement of Brașov as a location for major international companies. The combination of a high-quality newly delivered building, strong local infrastructure and the industrial park’s strategic position all met Airbus’ requirements, while offering flexibility for future growth both at CTPark Brașov and across CTP’s wider network. The partnerships we have with clients at CTP go far beyond providing space alone. As a developer-landlord that holds its properties for the long term we create the conditions that allow our clients to develop and strategically evolve over time. We look forward to working with Airbus long into the future.”

CTPark Brașov currently comprises approximately 18,000 sqm of built space. There is a further 27,000 sqm of development potential at the park, totaling around 13 hectares for companies seeking space in one of Romania’s key industrial regions.

The agreement with Airbus further strengthens CTP’s position in Romania, one of its largest markets. CTP’s Romanian portfolio comprises more than 3.2 million sqm of logistics and industrial space across key logistics and manufacturing hubs, including in Bucharest, Timișoara, Brașov, Sibiu, Craiova and Arad. Romania accounts for more than 3.2 million sqm of CTP’s 15.1 million sqm European portfolio and remains one of the company’s most important growth markets across Central and Eastern Europe.

About CTP

CTP is Europe’s largest listed developer, owner, and operator of logistics and industrial real estate by gross leasable area ("GLA"), with a portfolio of 15.1 million sqm of GLA in 12 countries and 1.7 million sqm under construction as of 30 September 2026. The company’s ready-built factories and warehouses, together with its custom-built solutions, serve over 1,700 clients ranging from large blue-chip multinationals to local SMEs. CTP builds long-term partnerships through a client-first approach, maintaining roughly 93% annual retention and generating 63% of new business from existing client expansion. All new buildings are certified to the BREEAM standard "Very Good" or higher, underscoring the company’s commitment to sustainable development. CTP holds Investment Grade ratings from S&P: BBB (Stable), Moody’s: Baa2 (Stable), and JCR: A (Stable).

data.title: My wife pays thousands of dollars for her family to visit from Argentina. How can I convince her to stop?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'I don't want my wife to feel that I'm asking her to choose between me and her family'

"Hotel rooms can cost as much as $400 per night, and the total cost of these visits can easily run into several thousand dollars." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

My wife and I have a wonderful marriage, but there is one recurring issue that has become a significant source of frustration for me. While my wife is an exceptionally generous and giving person, I feel that some of her family members have come to take advantage of that generosity.

Several of her relatives regularly want to visit us in New York, traveling from Argentina. Given the long journey, these visits typically last around two weeks. Some of her nieces, nephews and siblings expect to visit virtually every year.

The problem is that we live in a Manhattan apartment with limited space, and hosting guests for extended periods is a significant imposition on our daily routines, privacy and overall quality of life. Now that we also have a baby, the logistical and personal challenges are even greater.

My wife is extremely devoted to her family and, for whatever reason, seems to have difficulty saying no to their requests. I've gently raised my concerns several times, explaining that we simply don't have the space to accommodate so many guests.

Many of her relatives have limited financial means, so my wife often ends up covering not only their flights and accommodations, but also airport transportation, meals, entertainment and other expenses.

Don't miss: My older brother, who has no children, cut our only sister out of his will. I'll get everything instead. Do I tell her?

Space constraints

While I appreciate that this addresses some of the space constraints, it creates a separate issue: the considerable financial burden. Hotel rooms can cost as much as $400 per night, and the total cost of these visits can easily run into several thousand dollars.

Although my wife has her own money, these expenditures still have meaningful opportunity costs for our family. We have substantial financial priorities, including the high cost of childcare in New York City, saving toward purchasing a home and planning for our son's education.

It's also worth noting that we already travel to Argentina every year to visit her family. So it's not as though declining to host relatives in New York would prevent us from maintaining close relationships with them or spending time together.

I love my wife and I genuinely admire her generosity and commitment to her family. However, I'm increasingly feeling that her relatives' expectations are being prioritized over my comfort in our own home, our privacy and our family's financial goals.

I'm concerned that if this continues, my frustration will turn into resentment and undermine what is otherwise an excellent marriage. How can I establish reasonable boundaries? I don't want my wife to feel that I'm asking her to choose between me and her family.

The Husband

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'It leaves me with a sour taste': My elderly mother gave our cousin $800 for a car repair. Should I be worried?

She could be afraid of angering or disappointing her relatives, issues that might be rooted in her upbringing and culture.

Dear Husband,

When words fail to change bad habits, enlist a pen and paper.

This is a domestic as well as a financial problem. Your wife is spending money in isolation and without keeping your overall financial goals in mind. You probably are too, perhaps in smaller ways. This bad habit, which only appears to be getting worse, needs to be broken.

The only way to accomplish this is to show her how much money these trips are costing your family, in real terms, as you also pay for childcare and rent, save for emergencies and your child's schooling and college education, and put money aside to buy a home.

Of course, making it personal will only get you both mired in hurt feelings and defensiveness, so you need to take her family out of the equation as much as possible and revisit your marriage vows - your pact to respect and honor each other.

You can have these conversations alone, or with the help of a financial adviser or counselor. I suggest the latter. A mediator can help you articulate your concerns, frame your questions as "I feel ..." rather than "You are ..." and prevent you from hurting each other's feelings.

Ultimately, you need to formulate a family policy rather than take potshots at your wife's family. You have reached a stage in your married life when you are working toward tangible financial goals, and spending thousands of dollars on third parties compromises that.

A financial therapist could help to field your concerns.

Emphasize your shared responsibility and the importance of working as a team. Hosting relatives every year impinges on your privacy and ability to relax in your own home, disrupts your daily routines and makes your responsibilities as new parents more challenging.

Eventually, your wife will have to find the words to say no to people, her family included. It's not always easy, but after you do it once, it gets easier. Given that she has set an unhealthy precedent, this conversation can start with a soft no - and the truth.

She can tell her family: "This year is impossible for us to host. We no longer have room. We have a young child and a lot of family and work commitments." For what it's worth, there's also a difference between relatives visiting your city and crashing at your place.

I feel confident that facing up to the reality of your financial situation will encourage your wife to stop spending money meant for your little family on visiting relatives. Hotels, theater tickets and meals all add up, and something is wrong if her family members all expect the royal treatment.

Any expenditure over $1,000 should have veto power.

Facing that reality means making big decisions together - and spending thousands of dollars a year on visiting relatives is categorically a big decision, even if it seems like it's actually lots of small acts of generosity. Any expenditure over $1,000 should be discussed and agreed upon.

Many couples have a "mutual veto" on a large purchase. Some have a dollar cap, the size of which depends on their income. Unless there are two yes votes, the veto kicks in. But a dollar cap of $1,000 doesn't mean you can spend $999 each on a bunch of relatives.

Finally, many couples have "yours, mine and ours" accounts. They have a joint account for shared bills, savings and vacation money, and smaller personal checking accounts for guilt-free "mad money" splurges. But everything is accounted for in the family ledger.

At the root of this problem is why your wife feels obliged to host her relatives. Our relationship with money is emotional and, although we probably don't like to acknowledge it, less logical than we might imagine. She could be afraid of angering or disappointing her family.

A financial therapist could help explore why your wife feels such a strong sense of familial duty, which may be rooted in her upbringing and culture. She may even feel guilty about having achieved a more financially comfortable life than her relatives.

Whatever the reason behind it, the open-house era of hosting relatives should come to a close.

Alibaba Group Announces September Quarter 2026 Results and Interim Results for the Six Months Ended September 30, 2026

Alibaba Group Holding Limited (NYSE: BABA and HKEX: 9988 (HKD Counter) and 89988 (RMB Counter), “Alibaba” or “Alibaba Group”) today announced its financial results for the quarter and the six months ended September 30, 2026.

“Our full-stack AI capabilities continue to improve commercialization and delivered a strong quarter. Growth in Alibaba Cloud’s recurring revenue from external customers was 67%, which drove an acceleration of overall cloud revenue growth with significantly improving profitability. AI-related product revenue delivered triple-digit growth for the thirteenth consecutive quarter. We recently announced comprehensive upgrades spanning proprietary chips, supernode architecture, agent-native cloud infrastructure, AI models and agents. Notably, T-Head unveiled its next-generation Zhenwu V900 AI chip. In our consumption business, Alibaba E-commerce Group’s profitability improved significantly. Quick commerce continued to narrow its losses substantially while maintaining market share,” said Eddie Wu, Chief Executive Officer of Alibaba Group. “We will continue to bring technological innovations to our comprehensive AI stack to meet the strong and diverse AI demands across industries.”

“This quarter, our business delivered strong growth in both revenue and earnings because of our strategic focus on AI + Cloud growth and profit sustainability in Alibaba E-commerce Group. Cloud segment revenue growth continued to accelerate, with quality earnings further driving EBITA margin up to 14.5%. The e-commerce segment delivered significant EBITA growth, driven by improving unit economics in quick commerce and solid growth of marketplace e-commerce,” said Toby Xu, Chief Financial Officer of Alibaba Group. “As AI monetization continues to ramp up, we will maintain disciplined investments in AI capabilities with a focus on return on invested capital while targeting to achieve positive free cash flow.”

BUSINESS HIGHLIGHTS

In the quarter ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenue was RMB271,519 million (US$40,498 million), an increase of 10% year-over-year.
  • AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue increased by 53% year-over-year. Revenue from external customers increased by 64% year-over-year, primarily attributable to a 67% growth in recurring revenue from external customers (excluding compute equipment solutions revenue), largely driven by the increasing adoption of AI-related products.
  • Customer management revenue decreased by 5% year-over-year. Excluding the contra revenue impact from the new business development program, customer management revenue on a like-for-like basis would have grown by 1% year-over-year.
  • Income from operations was RMB29,116 million (US$4,343 million), an increase of 443% year-over-year, primarily due to the increase in adjusted EBITA. Adjusted EBITA, a non-GAAP measurement, increased 260% year-over-year to RMB32,636 million (US$4,868 million), primarily attributable to the improved operating results in Taobao Instant Commerce and Cloud business, as well as operating efficiencies across various businesses, partly offset by our increased investment in technology.
  • Net income attributable to ordinary shareholders was RMB64,535 million (US$9,626 million). Net income was RMB64,420 million (US$9,608 million), an increase of 213% year-over-year, primarily attributable to the increase in net investment income and income from operations. Non-GAAP net income in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was RMB19,909 million (US$2,969 million), an increase of 92% compared to RMB10,352 million in the same quarter of 2025.
  • Diluted earnings per ADS was RMB25.94 (US$3.87). Diluted earnings per share was RMB3.24 (US$0.48 or HK$3.78). Non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS was RMB8.10 (US$1.21), an increase of 86% year-over-year. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share was RMB1.01 (US$0.15 or HK$1.18), an increase of 86% year-over-year.
  • Net cash provided by operating activities was RMB15,690 million (US$2,340 million), an increase of 55% compared to RMB10,099 million in the same quarter of 2025. Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measurement of liquidity, was an outflow of RMB34,472 million (US$5,142 million), compared to an outflow of RMB21,840 million in the same quarter of 2025. The decrease in free cash flow was mainly attributed to the increase in our cloud infrastructure expenditure, partly offset by reduced losses in Taobao Instant Commerce and increased customer prepayments for our cloud services. As of September 30, 2026, our cash and other liquid investments(1) were RMB487,929 million (US$72,776 million).

In the six months ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenue was RMB540,472 million (US$80,613 million), an increase of 9% year-over-year.
  • AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue increased by 49% year-over-year. Revenue from external customers increased by 56% year-over-year, primarily attributable to a 54% growth in recurring revenue from external customers (excluding compute equipment solutions revenue), which was largely driven by the increasing adoption of AI-related products.
  • Customer management revenue decreased by 6% year-over-year. Excluding the contra revenue impact from the new business development program, customer management revenue on a like-for-like basis would have grown by 1% year-over-year.
  • Income from operations was RMB44,277 million (US$6,604 million), an increase of 10% year-over-year, primarily due to the increase in adjusted EBITA, partly offset by the increase in impairment of goodwill, and a provision(2) recorded this year. Adjusted EBITA, a non-GAAP measurement, increased 25% year-over-year to RMB59,965 million (US$8,944 million), primarily attributable to the improved operating results in Taobao Instant Commerce and Cloud business, as well as operating efficiencies across various businesses, partly offset by our increased investment in technology.
  • Net income attributable to ordinary shareholders was RMB75,072 million (US$11,197 million). Net income was RMB74,864 million (US$11,166 million), an increase of 19% year-over-year, primarily attributable to the increase in net investment income and income from operations. Non-GAAP net income was RMB40,624 million (US$6,059 million), a decrease of 7% compared to RMB43,862 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Diluted earnings per ADS was RMB29.91 (US$4.46). Diluted earnings per share was RMB3.74 (US$0.56 or HK$4.36). Non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS was RMB16.62 (US$2.48), a decrease of 13% year-over-year. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share was RMB2.08 (US$0.31 or HK$2.42), a decrease of 13% year-over-year.
  • Net cash provided by operating activities was RMB38,635 million (US$5,763 million), an increase of 26% compared to RMB30,771 million in the same period of 2025. Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measurement of liquidity, was an outflow of RMB79,142 million (US$11,804 million), compared to an outflow of RMB40,655 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease in free cash flow was mainly attributed to the increase in our cloud infrastructure expenditure, partly offset by reduced losses in Taobao Instant Commerce and increased customer prepayments for our cloud services. As of September 30, 2026, our cash and other liquid investments(1) were RMB487,929 million (US$72,776 million).

Reconciliations of GAAP measures to non-GAAP measures presented above are included at the end of this results announcement.

BUSINESS AND STRATEGIC UPDATES

Alibaba E-commerce Group

During the quarter, we sustained revenue stability with CMR decreasing 5% year-over-year and growing 1% on a like-for-like basis if the contra revenue impact from the new business development program were excluded. Adjusted EBITA of the group achieved 243% year-over-year growth this quarter, primarily driven by a significant loss reduction in the China Quick Commerce business. In addition, our China E-commerce business contributed to stable operating profit and the Global Wholesale business delivered strong profits, while we reduced losses in the International E-commerce business.

We have continued to advance our strategic priorities of unlocking significant synergies across our domestic and cross-border businesses, and deepening the integration of AI capabilities across our e-commerce platforms. Recent progress includes the integration of management across our domestic and international wholesale businesses, as well as the launch of QwenWork E-commerce for merchants, an AI product powered by our agentic AI capabilities, in October.

QwenWork E-commerce is integrated into QwenWork, our one-stop AI agent platform, and is designed to automate end-to-end merchant workflows, including store operations, business analytics, advertising and customer service. Leveraging our existing merchant tools, it connects directly to Taobao and Tmall data and will further support data access across other platforms, enabling more seamless cross-platform operations. In addition, by leveraging Qwen model family’s advanced multimodal capabilities, we are able to better understand complex consumer needs and deliver more relevant product recommendations with knowledge-based reasoning. These enhanced capabilities have driven a notable increase in general knowledge-related queries, creating more opportunities to identify latent consumer demand, facilitate product discovery, and drive sales conversion.

In our China Quick Commerce business, Taobao Instant Commerce continued to improve its unit economics quarter-over-quarter while maintaining market share. This reflected higher average order value, as we further improved the order mix through an increasing focus on high-value food and non-food categories. Meanwhile, Freshippo maintained its robust growth across online and offline channels, driven by deeper collaboration with Taobao Instant Commerce and the expansion of its multi-format store network that offers differentiated products to diverse demographics.

The number of 88VIP members, our highest spending consumer group, continued to increase by double digits year-over-year to approximately 66 million as of September 30, 2026. The ARPU of new 88VIP members, defined as those who joined the membership program within the past year, increased significantly year-over-year during the 11.11 Global Shopping Festival. We remain focused on the growth and retention of 88VIP members through enhanced value proposition to our most valued customers.

Xianyu is China’s leading consumer-to-consumer community and marketplace for idle goods. It makes buying and selling more convenient for consumers and small businesses through AI-powered features including smart pricing, automated product listing descriptions and precise buyer targeting, as well as consignment services. This quarter, Xianyu continued its strong growth momentum, with daily active users and paid orders up 23% and 29% year-over-year, respectively.

AI Cloud and Compute Services

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, revenue from AI Cloud and Compute Services was RMB60,973 million (US$9,094 million), a 53% increase from the same quarter last year. The growth of revenue from external customers accelerated to 64% year-over-year. The growth of recurring revenue from external customers, which excludes compute equipment solutions revenue, also accelerated to 67% year-over-year. In particular, AI-related product revenue continued to show strong momentum, achieving RMB17,918 million (US$2,673 million) and delivering the thirteenth consecutive quarter of triple-digit year-over-year growth. The strong growth reflected broad-based demand for our AI + Cloud services. Beyond training and inference workloads at AI labs, customers across the internet, automotive, embodied AI, financial services and biotechnology sectors rapidly expanded their use of our cloud services to support innovation and grow their business.

Cloud

Alibaba Cloud continued to strengthen our market-leading full-stack AI capabilities, as demonstrated by the comprehensive upgrades unveiled at the Apsara Conference in September, spanning proprietary chips, supernode architecture, agent-native cloud infrastructure, AI models and agents. These advancements across our co-designed and integrated stack have accelerated enterprise adoption and deeper integration into core business workflows, enabling us to capitalize on increasingly diverse demand across industries.

Our ability to empower enterprise AI adoption has earned notable recognition in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Strategic Cloud Platform Services, a report that comprehensively evaluates how cloud service providers support the entire enterprise cloud lifecycle. Alibaba Cloud was named a Leader in the highest quadrant, making it the first and only Asia-Pacific provider to receive this distinction.

Chip Design – T-Head Semiconductor (“T-Head”)

By rapidly advancing its portfolio of proprietary chips and software, T-Head further strengthened the infrastructure foundation underpinning our AI capabilities.

At the Apsara Conference in September, we unveiled the Zhenwu V900, our next-generation AI chip for training and inference, with commercial release scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. Built on our proprietary parallel computing architecture, the Zhenwu V900 delivers significant performance improvements over its predecessor, the Zhenwu M890. We also open-sourced T-Head SAIL, the software stack for Zhenwu chips, to simplify application migration, expand developer adoption, and strengthen compatibility with mainstream AI frameworks.

In addition, we launched the Zhenwu M890 supernode instance in August, marking the introduction of China’s first supernode architecture capable of supporting inference for models with more than two trillion parameters. At the Apsara Conference, we also showcased our next-generation supernode product, which integrates the Zhenwu V900 with other proprietary interconnect, networking, and storage chips, and is scheduled for launch in the first quarter of 2027.

AI Labs and Applications

Model

We continued to advance our comprehensive model portfolio, with a primary focus on foundation models, while enhancing capabilities across video, audio, image and music. This demonstrates our industry leadership and rapid pace of iteration.

Recently, we launched Qwen4-Max, built on the new mixture-of-experts architecture with 2.4 trillion backbone parameters and native visual capabilities. Qwen4-Max advances productivity and token efficiency, delivering stronger long-horizon task execution across industries, including manufacturing, game development, healthcare, and frontier scientific research.

QwenWork

Our agentic platform QwenWork continued to gain traction across industries, driven by ongoing enhancements to its enterprise capabilities. At the Apsara Conference in September, we launched Enterprise Context, a solution that continuously organizes and updates enterprise information and knowledge across company documents, meeting records and internal communications. It enables AI agents to access company-specific information and execute tasks based on organizational knowledge and workflows.

Qwen App

Qwen app for individual users now provides personalized assistance for tasks across more than 20 service categories, including shopping, local services, travel, work, learning, personal finance and health, leveraging Alibaba’s ecosystem and third-party partnerships. In October, we launched Qwen Go!, a cloud-based personal agent embedded within the Qwen app. Qwen Go! autonomously executes multi-step tasks across platforms, while retaining contextual information and user preferences over time to deliver increasingly personalized assistance across everyday activities.

All Others

Our store guide and mapping platform Amap offers consumers one-stop access to services such as navigation, to-destination services and ride-hailing. On October 1, 2026, the first day of National Day holiday in China, Amap recorded an all-time high of approximately 370 million peak daily active users. Leveraging Amap Street Stars, a feature that provides a trust-based rating system to support users’ consumption decisions, Amap has strengthened its mindshare in local services across consumption use cases, including dining, tourist attractions and seasonal activities.

Share Repurchases

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, we repurchased a total of 17.95 million ordinary shares (equivalent to approximately 2.24 million ADSs) for a total of US$221 million. These purchases were made in the U.S. market under our share repurchase program.

Capital Expenditures

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, capital expenditures were RMB50,477 million (US$7,529 million), an increase of 60% compared to RMB31,501 million in the same quarter of 2025, due to continued investments in AI infrastructure to meet strong and accelerating customer demand. The significant year-over-year increase was due to an acceleration in scaling compute capacity, higher pricing of a broad range of chip components, an increase in CPU-compute capacity driven by anticipated growing customer adoption of AI agents, and fluctuations in procurement cycles.

In addition to training and inference demand from AI Labs, we continue to see robust demand from customers in China’s emerging innovation economy, including electric vehicles (EVs), embodied AI, and biotechnology. Scale is becoming an increasingly critical competitive advantage in cloud computing, providing us with orchestration flexibility, operating efficiency and cost advantages. By investing in infrastructure today, we aim to extend our scale leadership, strengthen our supply chain and reinforce our long-term competitive position.

Cost of revenue – Cost of revenue in the six months ended September 30, 2026 was RMB334,572 million (US$49,903 million), or 61.9% of revenue, compared to RMB287,210 million, or 58.0% of revenue, in the same period of 2025. Without the effect of share-based compensation expense, cost of revenue as a percentage of revenue would have increased from 57.8% in the same period of 2025 to 61.7% in the six months ended September 30, 2026, primarily driven by the increase in proportion of cloud and technology businesses in our revenue mix, as well as the contra revenue impact from the new business development program, partly offset by the increase in operating efficiency of Taobao Instant Commerce.

Product development expenses – Product development expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2026 were RMB45,161 million (US$6,736 million), or 8.4% of revenue, compared to RMB32,096 million, or 6.5% of revenue, in the same period of 2025. Without the effect of share-based compensation expense, product development expenses as a percentage of revenue would have increased from 5.9% in the same period of 2025 to 7.8% in the six months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to our increased investments in technology, as well as research and development personnel.

Sales and marketing expenses – Sales and marketing expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2026 were RMB88,966 million (US$13,269 million), or 16.5% of revenue, compared to RMB119,674 million, or 24.2% of revenue, in the same period of 2025. Without the effect of share-based compensation expense, sales and marketing expenses as a percentage of revenue would have decreased from 24.0% in the same period of 2025 to 16.3% in the six months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to more efficient investment in Taobao Instant Commerce and the impact of our new business development program, where relevant subsidies previously recorded as sales and marketing expenses are now recorded as contra revenue item.

General and administrative expenses – General and administrative expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2026 were RMB22,805 million (US$3,401 million), or 4.2% of revenue, compared to RMB14,778 million, or 3.0% of revenue, in the same period of 2025. Without the effect of share-based compensation expense, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of revenue would have increased from 2.6% in the same period of 2025 to 3.8% in the six months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to a provision in relation to the fine imposed by the European Commission under the Digital Services Act of EUR550 million recorded this year.

Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITA

Adjusted EBITDA increased 35% year-over-year to RMB85,198 million (US$12,708 million) in the six months ended September 30, 2026, compared to RMB62,991 million in the same period of 2025. Adjusted EBITA increased 25% year-over-year to RMB59,965 million (US$8,944 million) in the six months ended September 30, 2026, compared to RMB47,917 million in the same period of 2025, primarily attributable to the improved operating results in Taobao Instant Commerce and Cloud business, as well as operating efficiencies across various businesses, partly offset by our increased investment in technology. A reconciliation of net income to adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITA is included at the end of this results announcement.

Net income and Non-GAAP net income

Our net income in the six months ended September 30, 2026 was RMB74,864 million (US$11,166 million), compared to RMB62,994 million in the same period of 2025, primarily attributable to the increase in net investment income and income from operations.

Excluding non-cash share-based compensation expense, gains/losses of investments, impairment of goodwill and intangible assets, and certain other items, non-GAAP net income in the six months ended September 30, 2026 was RMB40,624 million (US$6,059 million), a decrease of 7% compared to RMB43,862 million in the same period of 2025. A reconciliation of net income to non-GAAP net income is included at the end of this results announcement.

Net income attributable to ordinary shareholders

Net income attributable to ordinary shareholders in the six months ended September 30, 2026 was RMB75,072 million (US$11,197 million), compared to RMB64,106 million in the same period of 2025, primarily attributable to the increase in net investment income and income from operations.

Diluted earnings per ADS/share and non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS/share

Diluted earnings per ADS in the six months ended September 30, 2026 was RMB29.91 (US$4.46), compared to RMB26.73 in the same period of 2025. Excluding non-cash share-based compensation expense, gains/losses of investments, impairment of goodwill and intangible assets, and certain other items, non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS in the six months ended September 30, 2026 was RMB16.62 (US$2.48), a decrease of 13% compared to RMB19.10 in the same period of 2025.

Diluted earnings per share in the six months ended September 30, 2026 was RMB3.74 (US$0.56 or HK$4.36), compared to RMB3.34 in the same period of 2025. Excluding non-cash share-based compensation expense, gains/losses of investments, impairment of goodwill and intangible assets, and certain other items, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share in the six months ended September 30, 2026 was RMB2.08 (US$0.31 or HK$2.42), a decrease of 13% compared to RMB2.39 in the same period of 2025.

A reconciliation of diluted earnings per ADS/share to non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS/share is included at the end of this results announcement. Each ADS represents eight ordinary shares.

Cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments and other treasury investments

As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments and other treasury investments included in equity securities and other investments on the consolidated balance sheets, of which that are unrestricted for withdrawal and use, were RMB487,929 million (US$72,776 million), compared to RMB520,824 million as of March 31, 2026. Other treasury investments consist of fixed deposits, certificates of deposit and marketable debt securities with original maturities over one year for treasury purposes. The decrease of RMB32,895 million during the six months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily due to free cash flow outflow of RMB79,142 million (US$11,804 million), dividend payment of RMB16,648 million (US$2,483 million), partly offset by net proceeds from placing of new shares of HK$80 billion.

Net cash provided by operating activities and free cash flow

During the six months ended September 30, 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was RMB38,635 million (US$5,763 million), an increase of 26% compared to RMB30,771 million in the same period of 2025. Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measurement of liquidity, was an outflow of RMB79,142 million (US$11,804 million), compared to an outflow of RMB40,655 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease in free cash flow was mainly attributed to the increase in our cloud infrastructure expenditure, partly offset by reduced losses in Taobao Instant Commerce and increased customer prepayments for our cloud services. A reconciliation of net cash provided by operating activities to free cash flow is included at the end of this results announcement.

Net cash used in investing activities

During the six months ended September 30, 2026, net cash used in investing activities of RMB38,795 million (US$5,786 million) primarily reflected capital expenditures of RMB118,155 million (US$17,623 million), partly offset by a net decrease in short-term investments and other treasury investments by RMB70,805 million (US$10,561 million), and net cash inflow of RMB7,303 million (US$1,089 million) for investment and acquisition activities.

Net cash provided by financing activities

During the six months ended September 30, 2026, net cash provided by financing activities of RMB62,164 million (US$9,272 million) primarily reflected net proceeds from placing of new shares of HK$80 billion and net proceeds from bank borrowings of RMB14,802 million (US$2,208 million), partly offset by dividend payment of RMB16,648 million (US$2,483 million).

NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES

To supplement our consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP, we use the following non-GAAP financial measures: for our consolidated results, adjusted EBITDA (including adjusted EBITDA margin), adjusted EBITA (including adjusted EBITA margin), non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share/ADS and free cash flow. For more information on these non-GAAP financial measures, please refer to the table captioned “Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Measures to the Nearest Comparable U.S. GAAP Measures” in this results announcement.

We believe that adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITA, non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share/ADS help identify underlying trends in our business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain income or expenses that we include in income from operations, net income and diluted earnings per share/ADS. We believe that these non-GAAP measures provide useful information about our core operating results, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by our management in its financial and operational decision-making. We present three different income measures, namely adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITA and non-GAAP net income in order to provide more information and greater transparency to investors about our operating results.

We consider free cash flow to be a liquidity measure that provides useful information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated by our business that can be used for strategic corporate transactions, including investing in our new business initiatives, making strategic investments and acquisitions and strengthening our balance sheet.

Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITA, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share/ADS and free cash flow should not be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to income from operations, net income, diluted earnings per share/ADS, cash flows or any other measure of performance or as an indicator of our operating performance. These non-GAAP financial measures presented here do not have standardized meanings prescribed by U.S. GAAP and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies. Other companies may calculate similarly titled measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures to our data.

Adjusted EBITDA represents net income before interest and investment income, net, interest expense, other income (expense), net, income tax expenses, share of results of equity method investees, certain non-cash expenses, consisting of share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, impairment of goodwill, depreciation and impairment of property and equipment, and operating lease cost relating to land use rights, and others (including provision in relation to matters outside the ordinary course of business), which we do not believe are reflective of our core operating performance during the periods presented.

Adjusted EBITA represents net income before interest and investment income, net, interest expense, other income (expense), net, income tax expenses, share of results of equity method investees, certain non-cash expenses, consisting of share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, impairment of goodwill, and others (including provision in relation to matters outside the ordinary course of business), which we do not believe are reflective of our core operating performance during the periods presented.

Non-GAAP net income represents net income before non-cash share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, gain or loss on deemed disposals/disposals/revaluation of investments, impairment of goodwill and investments, and others (including provision in relation to matters outside the ordinary course of business), and adjustments for the tax effects.

Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share represents non-GAAP net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by the weighted average number of outstanding ordinary shares, in each case for computing non-GAAP diluted earnings per share on a diluted basis. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS represents non-GAAP diluted earnings per share after adjusting for the ordinary share-to-ADS ratio.

Free cash flow represents net cash provided by operating activities as presented in our consolidated cash flow statement less purchases of property and equipment (excluding acquisition of land use rights and construction in progress relating to office campuses) and intangible assets (excluding those acquired through acquisitions), as well as adjustments to exclude from net cash provided by operating activities the buyer protection fund deposits from merchants on our marketplaces. We deduct certain items of cash flows from investing activities in order to provide greater transparency into cash flow from our revenue-generating business operations. We exclude “acquisition of land use rights and construction in progress relating to office campuses” because the office campuses are used by us for corporate and administrative purposes and are not directly related to our revenue-generating business operations. We also exclude buyer protection fund deposits from merchants on our marketplaces because these deposits are restricted for the purpose of compensating buyers for claims against merchants.

The table captioned “Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Measures to the Nearest Comparable U.S. GAAP Measures” in this results announcement has more details on the non-GAAP financial measures that are most directly comparable to GAAP financial measures and the related reconciliations between these financial measures.

data.title: The real beneficiary of the AI tech revolution fueled by Anthropic may surprise you
data.description:
By Jules Rimmer

India will benefit from the AI revolution, without having to make the upfront investment

"The real test for AI will be on the streets of Mumbai and thousands of cities like it, not the frontier labs of San Francisco," says a Deutsche Bank analyst.

Who is going to be the real winner of the artificial-intelligence revolution? It might surprise investors to discover that the asset class most likely to reap the rewards of artificial intelligence has flown under the radar until now: step forward India.

A new report from Deutsche Bank analyst Adrian Cox was published Thursday, coinciding with the high-profile listing on Nasdaq of Anthropic (ANT), one of the two most important frontier AI labs beside OpenAI. Cox's research suggests India will demonstrate that creating a new technology matters less than adopting it at scale.

India doesn't produce that much homegrown technology but it has a vast, tech-savvy and, crucially, young population that can exploit what the frontier labs are creating. This realization has dawned on markets in recent weeks as India's low correlation with the AI trade has suddenly come to the fore and proved a distinct advantage.

Looking at the relative performance of Indian and U.S. trading bourses in the last six weeks or so is instructive: the markets have got wind of this, as India's Nifty 50 IN:NIFTY50 has surged while the Nasdaq 100 NDX has slumped.

The iShares MSCI India ETF INDA has jumped 9% just this month.

Cox points out that while the U.S. and China have the models, the chips and the trillions of dollars of data-center capex, "India has 1.5 billion potential users, digital rails that are already built, an enormous tech workforce and some of the world's largest unmet needs in finance, health care and agriculture,"

To that point, India recently became ChatGPT's largest market by weekly users. To illustrate the opportunity, Cox cites the example of a "street vendor selling a single piece of fruit will typically hold up a QR code on their phone for instant payment." For Cox this suggests, "the real test for AI will not be in the frontier labs of San Francisco but on streets like these in Mumbai."

India's advantage is that it can adopt the infrastructure-light approach, no need for hundreds of billions of dollars invested in models and data centers and chips. "It can plug off the shelf software into well-developed national digital systems, tapping into the world's largest population with a median age of 29."

Despite its low profile in the AI buildout bonanza, India ranks third in the Stanford Global AI Vibrancy Tool, a measure of how much and how successfully various countries are adopting AI.

India ranks third in the Stanford Global AI Vibrancy Tool

In recent weeks inflows to the Indian equity market have picked up. Citi highlighted India had absorbed $4.9 billion of inflows in the second week of November after seeing $1.7 billion in flows during the first week of the month.

In its 2027 outlook published Tuesday, Goldman Sachs upgraded India to overweight, saying its strong domestic demand, robust earnings and decade-low foreign positioning make the country an attractive AI diversifier.

-Jules Rimmer

data.title: Stock Futures Rise as Optimism Improves Ahead of Anthropic Trading Debut
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Nasdaq futures led a rally in U.S. stocks premarket, after Anthropic's pricing of its hotly anticipated listing lifted confidence around the artificial-intelligence trade.

Anthropic's expectation-beating IPO pricing helped investor focus shift away from the AI jitters that have weighed on stocks so far this week. However, sentiment was tempered by hawkish Federal Reserve meeting minutes Wednesday that added to fears of extended policy tightening.

Nasdaq futures jumped 1.9% as chip makers and cloud-computing stocks rallied premarket. Anthropic sold more shares at a higher price than anticipated, implying a value of $1.5 trillion for the company. S&P 500 futures were also in the green--up 1.1%--as the index looks to turn the tide on a fifth-straight day of losses. Contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.6%. The index has fallen by more than 1% for three days in a row.

Equities were mixed across Asia, where the tech-dominated Nikkei Stock Average in Japan and South Korea's Kospi both closed in the green. Stock indexes in Hong Kong and Shanghai fell, however. In Europe, major indexes were all in the green. The continent-wide Stoxx 600 rose 0.5%.

Treasury yields ticked higher after falling in Asian trade, as investors respond to a hawkish readout from the Fed's October meeting. Near-term rate-sensitive two-year yields rose above 4.800%, while 10-year yields nudged back toward 5.100%. Thirty-year yields hovered around 5.420%.

Oil prices ticked slightly higher, picking up from falls Wednesday after U.S. crude oil inventories rose for a second consecutive week. The benchmark Brent crude contract rose 0.5% to trade around $92.40 a barrel, while the West Texas Intermediate contract nudged up 0.4% to trade around $83.50 a barrel.

The dollar fell slightly, but remained close to its highest level against a basket of global currencies since January 2025. Copper prices steadied after falling sharply in the last session but gold extended losses, trading close to $3,700 a troy ounce. Bitcoin rallied after recent declines, adding 2% to trade around $63,750.

Anthropic's trading debut will be in focus for the day ahead. Investors will also watch for readouts from the trilateral meeting between President Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.
